lessons: Keep hooks under 15 words and present a surprising, counter-intuitive premise immediately to secure 1.0+ retention at 10%
Avoid starting with direct repetition of video titles or excessively long introductory context, which causes early drop-offs around the 11-13% mark
Eliminate mid-video narrative stagnation and redundant descriptive padding; data shows sharpest viewer drop-offs occur at points of dense, repetitive explanatory lines
Structure scripts to maintain high pacing through the 50% mark, as videos with stronger mid-point retention (like the T. rex running and vision tests at 0.49 and 0.41) perform better overall
worst_moment_types: Dense, repetitive explanatory text blocks that slow down the narrative flow
Over-explaining basic mechanics immediately after the hook instead of moving to the core revelation
best_hook_types: Direct comparative thought experiments featuring relatable objects (cars, body parts)
Challenging deeply ingrained pop-culture assumptions right at the start
